A CPU cache is a small, fast memory located close to the CPU that stores frequently accessed data and instructions to reduce the time required to access them from main memory. It operates on the principle of locality, which includes temporal and spatial locality. Temporal locality refers to the tendency of a program to reuse data or instructions recently accessed, while spatial locality refers to the tendency to access data from nearby memory locations.
